diagnostic_evidence.quote: the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: Set a=θ·(x−x0), c=θ^⊥·(x−x0), b=t−t0. Then v0 v1 v2^2 = H3 H1 H2 = τ^{3/2}(cutoffs) e^{−τQ}, where Q = ½[(b−a)^2+(b+a)^2+(b−c)^2] = a^2 + (3/2)b^2 − bc + ½c^2. This is not a^2+b^2+c^2. For any three such unit-speed plane waves the b^2 coefficient is 3/2, so the claimed isotropic Gaussian is impossible. The quadratic form has determinant 1/2, so ∫τ^{3/2}e^{−τQ} = √2 π^{3/2}. By the integral identity, the right-hand limit therefore equals 3!·√2·π^{3/2} q(x0,t0), not 3!π^{3/2} q(x0,t0). Lemma (approx identity q) covers only isotropic Gaussians, so it does not apply as invoked.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed product with τ^{3/2}e^{−τQ} for the correct Q. Apply Lemma (approx identity q) after the linear change of variables z ↦ A^{1/2}z, where det A = 1/2. Correct the constant in (recoequ pw) to 3!√2π^{3/2}, and rescale the pointwise numerical results.
issues.overall_effect: The stated pointwise reconstruction formula overestimates q by a factor √2. Pointwise reconstructions computed with it are mis-scaled, which affects the pointwise-vs-Radon comparison.
issues.title: Pointwise product is an anisotropic Gaussian, so the pointwise reconstruction constant is wrong by a factor sqrt(2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine Gaussian computation and change of variables. The method, the convergence and the rate all survive; only a constant changes.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: lemma: reguderis relation of any two

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Triangle inequality and Lemmas~\ref{lemma: reguderis relation of any two} and \ref{lemma: reguderis relation of exact and regu}.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem bounds the error of R_α^{(p)}(g_δ) without restricting α, so as stated the bound is asserted for every α>0. This is false. With g_δ=g and α→∞, the left side tends to ||g^{(p)}||, which exceeds (||g||_{H^s}+C_p)δ^{1−p/s} for small δ when s>p. The proof cites both lemmas, and each holds only under α=δ^{2/s}, a hypothesis the theorem never states.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Fourier transforms are computed via the fast Fourier transform (FFT), which assumes periodic data.
We also give rigorous justification and stability estimates for the regularized spectral differentiation of noisy measurements.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the theorem justifies the choice of α 'in our case'. The reconstruction needs the point value R_α^{(3)}g̃(0), computed by FFT for a periodized function of ε1 on [−ε,ε]. The theorem only bounds an L^2(R) norm of the whole derivative for functions in H^s(R) with L^2(R) noise. An L^2 bound does not control a point value, and a nonzero periodic extension is not in L^2(R). The noise model ||E(f)||_{L^2(Σ)} ≤ δ also does not translate directly into the theorem's L^2(R) hypothesis. The paper therefore establishes no error bound or justified parameter choice for the quantity actually computed.

failure_location.quote: In our case Theorem~\ref{thm: reguderis error estimate for Gaussian} gives a theoretically justified choice for the regularization parameter $\alpha>0$ depending on the error level $\delta>0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a pointwise, periodic analogue. For example, bound |g'''(0) − R_α^{(3)}g̃(0)| through ∫|ξ|^p e^{−αξ^2}|ĝ−ĝ_δ| and the bias term, under s > p+1/2. This yields a different rate and choice of α. Alternatively, restrict the claim to the L^2(R) setting.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised rigorous justification of the regularized differentiation step does not cover the reconstruction step R_α^{(3)}g̃(0). The noise-to-error behaviour of the Radon reconstruction is left without theoretical support.
issues.title: L^2(R) stability theorem does not justify the pointwise, periodized derivative used in the reconstruction
issues.why_classification: Closing the gap needs a new contained lemma with a different rate, or a withdrawal of the claimed justification. It does not need new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$
we set the auxiliary function $v_0$ corresponding to $(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0)$
in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$

issues.failure_explanation: For Ω=[−0.5,0.5]^2 we have r=√2/2, so the admissible times satisfy [t1,t2] ⊂ (1.414, 1.586). The implementation uses t0 = T/2+η0 ∈ [1.1, 1.9], so W_0 is not in W_Radon. The sharper requirement also fails at the edge. For η0=0.4 and θ0=(1,1)/√2 (45° ∈ Θ'), H_2(x,T) = H(−x·θ0 − 0.7). Its argument vanishes at x·θ0 = −0.7, which lies inside Ω, and φ_h(0)=1. Hence H_2(·,T) ≢ 0, so v_0 ≠ H_2 and the product approximation underlying the reconstruction formula is not justified there.

failure_location.quote: Let us now consider the reconstruction of $\radonR(q)$ for a set of parameters $W_0 \in W_{\text{Radon}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose T and P so that the parameters satisfy the admissibility conditions. At least enforce t0 − η0 > r + h and T − t0 − η0 > r + h, for example by slightly shrinking P or enlarging T. Then restate the admissible set accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification of the Radon reconstruction does not cover the parameters used in the experiments; it fails for extreme η0 at diagonal angles.
issues.title: Numerical Radon parameters lie outside the stated admissible set; final condition for v_0 fails at the sinogram edge
issues.why_classification: A local change of numerical parameters, or a restated admissibility condition, restores consistency without changing the method or its claims.
